        <commentText>This Amendment No. 8 to Schedule 13D (this "Amendment No. 8"), relating to the shares of common stock, par value $0.0001 per share ("Common Stock"), of CDT Equity Inc., a Delaware corporation formerly known as Conduit Pharmaceuticals Inc. (the "Issuer"), amends and supplements the Schedule 13D (the "Original Schedule 13D"), originally filed by the reporting persons named therein with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Commission") on September 29, 2023, as amended by Amendment No. 1 to the Original Schedule 13D, filed by such reporting persons with the Commission on September 19, 2024 ("Amendment No. 1"), as amended by Amendment No. 2 to the Original Schedule 13D, filed by such reporting persons with the Commission on July 31, 2025 ("Amendment No. 2"), as amended by Amendment No. 3 to the Original Schedule 13D, filed by such reporting persons with the Commission on September 22, 2025 ("Amendment No. 3"), as amended by Amendment No. 4 to the Original Schedule 13D, filed by such reporting persons with the Commission on December 22, 2025 ("Amendment No. 4"), as amended by Amendment No. 5 to the Original Schedule 13D, filed by such reporting persons with the Commission on May 14, 2026 ("Amendment No. 5") as amended by Amendment No. 6 to the Original Schedule 13D, filed by such reporting persons with the Commission on September 2, 2026 ("Amendment No. 6") as amended by Amendment No. 7 to the Original Schedule 13D, filed by such reporting persons with the Commission on October 27, 2026 ("Amendment No. 7  and, together with the Original Schedule 13D, the "Schedule 13D"). Except as specifically amended below, all other provisions of the Schedule 13D remain in effect. Capitalized terms used herein but not defined herein have the respective meanings ascribed to them in the Schedule 13D. The information contained in "Item 1. Security and Issuer." of the Schedule 13D is not being amended by this Amendment No. 8.</commentText>
      </item1>
      <item2>
        <filingPersonName>"Item 2. Identity and Background." of the Schedule 13D is not being amended by this Amendment No. 8."</filingPersonName>
      </item2>
      <item3>
        <fundsSource>"Item 3. Source or Amount of Funds or Other Consideration." of the Schedule 13D is not being amended by this Amendment No. 8.</fundsSource>
      </item3>
      <item4>
        <transactionPurpose>"Item 4. Purpose of Transaction." of the Schedule 13D is hereby amended and restated by this Amendment No. 8 as follows:

The Reporting Persons acquired the shares of Common Stock for investment purposes. On November 5, 2026, Dr. Regan on behalf of Corvus delivered a letter to the Issuer's board of directors expressing its concerns with respect to the Issuer's current market valuation, capital raising activities and the value of its assets. In connection therewith, Corvus expressed its intent to propose an acquisition of all of the outstanding shares of Common Stock not already beneficially owned by the Reporting Persons at a purchase price of $2.00 per share. The Reporting Persons intend to engage with the Issuer's board of directors regarding such potential transaction and alternatives that may enhance stockholder value. In connection with the foregoing, Corvus also requested that the Issuer's board of directors (i) suspend the Issuer's at-the-market offering program while the board considers the matters raised in the letter, (ii) form a committee of independent directors, with its own legal counsel and financial adviser, to evaluate the potential transaction and other alternatives available to the Issuer, and (iii) strengthen the Issuer's independent oversight by appointing at least one additional independent director. No definitive agreement has been entered into with respect to any such potential transaction, and the November 5, 2026 letter does not constitute an offer, tender offer, solicitation of an offer to buy or sell securities, or solicitation of proxies or consents. Any potential transaction would be subject to, among other things, due diligence, the negotiation and execution of definitive documentation, the recommendation of the Issuer's independent directors and any required stockholder and regulatory approvals, as well as compliance with applicable securities laws. There can be no assurance that any proposal or transaction will be made, agreed upon or consummated.

The Reporting Persons intend to continue to review their investment in the Issuer on a continuing basis. Depending on various factors, including the Issuer's response to the matters described above, the Issuer's business, prospects and financial condition, market conditions and other factors deemed relevant by the Reporting Persons, the Reporting Persons may from time to time take such actions with respect to their investment in the Issuer as they deem appropriate, including engaging in discussions with the Issuer's board of directors, management, other stockholders or other interested parties concerning the potential transaction, strategic alternatives, the Issuer's capitalization, financing activities, corporate governance or other matters relating to the Issuer. Based upon such review and discussions, as well as general economic, market and industry conditions and prospects and the Reporting Persons' liquidity requirements and investment considerations, in addition to the potential transactions, the Reporting Persons may consider additional courses of action, including taking any of the actions specified in clauses (a) through (j) of Item 4 of Schedule 13D. Each Reporting Person reserves the right, at any time and from time to time, to review or reconsider its or his position and/or change its or his purpose and/or formulate plans or proposals with respect thereto.</transactionPurpose>

        <fundsSource>On April 6, 2026 (the "Closing Date"), the Issuer completed its acquisition of CFO Silvia, Inc. ("CFO Silvia") pursuant to the Agreement and Plan of Merger, dated as of February 9, 2026 (the "Silvia Merger Agreement"), by and among the Issuer, Silvia Merger Sub, Inc. ("Silvia Merger Sub"), CFO Silvia, Inflection Points Inc d/b/a Professional Capital Management,  a Delaware corporation ("Professional Capital Management" and, together with the Reporting Person, the "Sellers"), the Reporting Person, in his individual capacity, and the Reporting Person, solely in his capacity as stockholder representative (in such capacity, the "Stockholder Representative"). Pursuant to the Silvia Merger Agreement, Silvia Merger Sub merged with and into CFO Silvia, with CFO Silvia surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary of the Issuer (the "Silvia Merger"). At the effective time of the Silvia Merger, each issued and outstanding share of CFO Silvia common stock ("CFO Silvia Common Stock") was converted into the right to receive shares of Common Stock,  deposited in escrow (the "Escrow Shares") and up to 9,000,000 additional shares of Common Stock issuable as earnout consideration (the "Earnout Shares").

In the Silvia Merger, the Reporting Person, in his individual capacity as a Seller, received 3,638,580 shares of Common Stock in exchange for his shares of CFO Silvia Common Stock. An additional 435,644 shares of Common Stock issued in respect of the Reporting Person's shares of CFO Silvia Common Stock (the "Noor Escrow Shares") were deposited into an escrow account ("Escrow Account") with PNC Bank, National Association, as escrow agent (the "Escrow Agent"), pursuant to that certain Escrow Agreement, dated as of April 6, 2026, by and among the Issuer, Stockholder Representative, and the Escrow Agent (the "Escrow Agreement"). Pursuant to the Escrow Agreement the Stockholder Representative may direct the voting of the Noor Escrow Shares on behalf of the Reporting Person. In connection with the Silvia Merger, the Reporting Person was also granted the right to receive up to 4,356,450 of the Earnout Shares (the "Noor Earnout Shares"), subject to the conditions described in Item 6. The consideration for the shares of Common Stock received by the Reporting Person in the Silvia Merger was his shares of CFO Silvia Common Stock.

Since the Closing Date, the Reporting Person has received additional shares of Common Stock upon the vesting and settlement of restricted stock units ("RSUs") granted to him by the Issuer on May 19, 2026, under the ProCap Financial, Inc. 2025 Equity Incentive Plan (the "2025 Equity Incentive Plan"). Each RSU represents the right to receive one share of Common Stock upon vesting, in accordance with the terms of the award. Since the Closing Date, the Reporting Person received: (i) on July 7, 2026, 125,628 shares of Common Stock, of which 47,411 shares of Common Stock were withheld by the Issuer to satisfy tax withholding obligations; and (ii) on October 7, 2026, 125,628 shares of Common Stock, of which 45,000 shares of Common Stock were withheld by the Issuer to satisfy tax withholding obligations. The Reporting Person did not pay cash consideration for the shares received upon the vesting of such RSUs.

On October 19, 2026, the Reporting Person's beneficial ownership exceeded five percent of the outstanding Common Stock as a result of a reduction in the number of shares of Common Stock outstanding due to repurchases by the Issuer. The Reporting Person did not acquire additional shares of Common Stock in connection with that threshold-crossing event.

No borrowed funds or personal funds of the Reporting Person were used to acquire the shares of Common Stock reported in this Schedule 13D.</fundsSource>
      </item3>
      <item4>
        <transactionPurpose>The Reporting Person acquired the shares of Common Stock reported in this Schedule 13D (i) as consideration in the Silvia Merger in exchange for his equity interest in CFO Silvia, a company he co-founded and of which he served as President and Chief Executive Officer prior to the Silvia Merger, and (ii) as compensation for his services as an officer of the Issuer. Since the Closing Date, the Reporting Person has served as Chief Technology Officer of the Issuer, reporting to the Issuer's Chief Executive Officer. The Reporting Person is not a director of the Issuer.1

This Schedule 13D is being filed because the Reporting Person's beneficial ownership exceeded five percent of the outstanding Common Stock as a result of repurchases of Common Stock by the Issuer, as described in Item 3. The Reporting Person has not sold or tendered any shares of Common Stock to the Issuer in the Issuer's share repurchase program. As described in Item 6, the Silvia Merger Agreement restricts the Reporting Person, for a period of two years following the Closing Date, from participating in any repurchase by the Issuer of Common Stock.

The Reporting Person expects to acquire additional shares of Common Stock in the future upon the vesting and settlement of RSUs granted or to be granted to him under the Employment Agreement described in Item 6 and, if the applicable conditions are satisfied, upon the issuance of the Noor Earnout Shares. The Issuer may withhold shares of Common Stock to satisfy tax withholding obligations arising upon the vesting of such awards.

Except as set forth in this Item 4, the Reporting Person does not have any present plans or proposals that relate to or would result in any of the matters set forth in clauses (a) through (j) of Item 4 of Schedule 13D.

The Reporting Person intends to review his investment in the Issuer on a continuing basis. Subject to the Silvia Merger Lock-Up Agreement and the Silvia Merger Agreement restrictions described in Item 6, the Issuer's policies applicable to its officers and applicable law, the Reporting Person may in the future acquire additional securities of the Issuer or dispose of some or all of the securities of the Issuer that he beneficially owns and may change his plans or proposals with respect to any of the matters described in this Item 4.</transactionPurpose>
      </item4>

        <percentageOfClassSecurities>As of the date of this Schedule 13D, the Reporting Person beneficially owns 4,233,069 shares of Common Stock, representing approximately 5.6% of the outstanding Common Stock, all of which are held directly by the Reporting Person.       <item6>
        <contractDescription>The information set forth in Items 3, 4 and 5 is incorporated by reference into this Item 6.

Silvia Merger Agreement. The Reporting Person is a party to the Silvia Merger Agreement as a Seller and as the Stockholder Representative. Pursuant to the Silvia Merger Agreement, 900,000 Escrow Shares, including the 435,644 Noor Escrow Shares, were deposited into the Escrow Account, where they are to be held for 12 months following the Closing Date to secure the indemnification obligations of the Sellers and the holders of CFO Silvia simple agreements for future equity (together with the Sellers, the "Holders") under Article VIII of the Silvia Merger Agreement. Under the Silvia Merger Agreement, the Earnout Shares are issuable if, during the 5-year period following the Closing Date, the volume-weighted average trading price of the Common Stock over a specified 10-day period equals or exceeds $9.00 per share of Common Stock (subject to adjustment as provided in the Silvia Merger Agreement) (the "Purchaser Trading Price"). Issuance of the Noor Earnout Shares is additionally conditioned on the Reporting Person's continued employment with the Issuer or its affiliates (or his termination without cause) as of the Earnout Release Date (as defined in the Silvia Merger Agreement). For a period of two years following the Closing Date, the Holders, including the Reporting Person, are prohibited from participating in any repurchase by the Issuer of Common Stock. As Stockholder Representative, the Reporting Person is authorized to act on behalf of the Holders with respect to certain matters under the Silvia Merger Agreement.

Escrow Agreement. The Escrow Agreement governs the custody and disbursement of the 900,000 Escrow Shares, including the Noor Escrow Shares, which are maintained by the Issuer's transfer agent as a book-entry position registered in the name of the Escrow Agent for the benefit of the former CFO Silvia equityholders. Until the Escrow Shares are delivered to those equityholders (or returned or otherwise transferred to, or redeemed by, the Issuer), each equityholder is the beneficial owner of its applicable portion of the Escrow Shares and has all rights with respect to those shares other than the right of possession or transfer. The Escrow Agent is not required to vote the Escrow Shares. The Issuer has agreed to provide the Stockholder Representative with materials sent to the Issuer's stockholders generally and, upon the Stockholder Representative's written request delivered at least five business days before the applicable voting deadline, to execute and deliver proxies or other voting documentation with respect to the Escrow Shares in accordance with the Stockholder Representative's instructions, so as to permit the Stockholder Representative to direct the voting of the Escrow Shares on behalf of the equityholders. Any cash, stock, property or rights distributed in respect of the Escrow Shares, including cash dividends, are held by the Escrow Agent as part of the escrow funds for distribution to the applicable equityholders. The Escrow Agent will disburse Escrow Shares and other escrow funds only upon a joint written direction signed by authorized representatives of the Issuer and the Stockholder Representative or a final, non-appealable court or arbitral order. The Escrow Agreement terminates upon the distribution of all property held under it or upon an earlier joint written direction of the Issuer and the Stockholder Representative

Silvia Merger Lock-Up Agreement. In connection with the closing of the Silvia Merger, the Reporting Person entered into a lock-up agreement with the Issuer, dated April 6, 2026 (the "Silvia Merger Lock-Up Agreement"). Under the Silvia Merger Lock-Up Agreement, the shares of Common Stock received by the Reporting Person at the closing of the Silvia Merger and the Noor Escrow Shares are subject to transfer restrictions for a period ending on the later of (A) the six-month anniversary of the Closing Date and (B) the date on which the price of the Common Stock equals or exceeds $9.00 per share (subject to adjustment). The Noor Earnout Shares, if issued, will be subject to a separate six-month lock-up following the Earnout Release Date. The Silvia Merger Lock-Up Agreement contains customary exceptions, including for transfers to affiliates, family members and trusts and for tax obligations.

Silvia Merger Registration Rights Agreement. In connection with the Silvia Merger, the Issuer entered into a Registration Rights Agreement, dated as of April 6, 2026, with the Holders (the "Registration Rights Agreement"), pursuant to which the Issuer agreed to register the resale of the shares of Common Stock issued at the closing of the Silvia Merger, the Escrow Shares and the Earnout Shares, if issued. The Registration Rights Agreement provides for demand, short-form and piggyback registration rights, subject to customary limitations. Pursuant to the Registration Rights Agreement, a majority-in-interest of the then outstanding Registrable Securities (as defined in the Registration Rights Agreement) may make a written demand for registration of all or part of their Registrable Securities as soon as practicable, but not more than 45 days after the Issuer's receipt of the demand for registration. The Issuer will not be obligated to effect more than three registrations pursuant to a demand registration. Piggyback registration rights are subject to underwriter cutbacks, and the Registration Rights Agreement allows the Issuer to postpone or withdraw the filing or effectiveness of a piggyback registration at any time in its sole discretion. The Registration Rights Agreement also permits the Issuer, if in its good faith judgment a registration would be seriously detrimental to the Issuer, to defer such filing for a period of not more than 30 days; provided, however, that the Issuer will not defer its obligation in this manner more than once in any 12-month period. The Registration Rights Agreement includes customary indemnification and contribution provisions. Registration rights terminate with respect to a holder when such holder's shares may be sold without restriction under Rule 144, subject to customary conditions.

Employment Agreement and Equity Awards. The Reporting Person is party to an employment agreement with the Issuer, effective as of April 6, 2026 (the "Employment Agreement"), under which he serves as Chief Technology Officer. The Employment Agreement provides for annual restricted stock unit awards with an aggregate grant date fair market value of $1,000,000, with the number of units determined by dividing that amount by the fair market value of a share of Common Stock on the grant date, vesting in equal quarterly installments over four quarters, subject to continued employment. If the Reporting Person's employment is terminated without cause or he resigns for good reason, his equity awards continue to vest on a time basis for six months, and if such termination or resignation occurs within six months following a change in control, all of his unvested time-based equity awards will vest in full. The RSUs described in Item 3 were granted under the 2025 Equity Incentive Plan.

The foregoing descriptions of the Silvia Merger Agreement, the Silvia Merger Lock-Up Agreement, [the Escrow Agreement,] the Registration Rights Agreement, the Employment Agreement and the Incentive Plan do not purport to be complete and are qualified in their entirety by reference to the full text of such documents, which are filed or incorporated by reference as exhibits to this Schedule 13D.

Except as described in this Schedule 13D, there are no contracts, arrangements, understandings or relationships (legal or otherwise) between the Reporting Person and any other person with respect to any securities of the Issuer, including any pledge, margin loan, hedging or derivative arrangement or Rule 10b5-1 trading plan.</contractDescription>
